changes.reason: Option is unstated rather than drawn from elsewhere: the Mole never sings; birds sing at line 18 after he has left the house. Entry and execution both true of the row.

Line 22 (the rabbit at the gap) is a true detail from outside lines 14-15; wrong-scope names it. No cause is asked for, so chronology-collapse was misfiled. Execution checked against lines 14, 15, 22.
Spring-cleaning is the Mole's (line 1) moved onto the rabbit, who at line 22 asks for sixpence: attribute-transfer names it. Execution true.

en-vocab-neighbouring-sense holds, by its own description, 'only where the surrounding text fixes the sense decisively'. It does not here: lines 22-25 ARE a quarrel of sorts (the rabbit demands a toll, the Mole bowls him over and jeers), so the quarrel sense of 'row' is defensible. What makes the option wrong is its parties ('between two of the rabbits'), which this entry does not name. Closer to en-attribute-transfer (the row moved onto two rabbits) or the old en-plausible-not-stated.
Nothing says the meadow was new to him; line 29 says 'never ... seen a river before' only of the river. Plausible-not-stated names it; execution true (line 15 has him rolling in the meadow).

The writer's figure (river as animal, line 30) is turned into the Mole's belief: the writer's choice read as the character's state, which is what the entry names. Line 33 'bewitched, entranced' checked.

The comparison at lines 34-35 is a very small child trotting beside a storyteller; trotting at a grown-up's side is the small child's hurrying to keep pace, carried onto the Mole. That is the vehicle's quality given for the subject's. Execution true of lines 34-35.
The face (line 48) is from after lines 43-45; the stem asks what he noticed first within 43-45. Wrong-scope names it; no cause asked, so chronology-collapse was misfiled.
The writer's detail-at-a-time reveal is turned into a feeling in the Mole; lines 48-52 give him no feeling. That is the writer's choice read as the character's state. Execution true.
'Dark and dirty with earth' is no sense of 'grave' and no word it resembles; it is what a burial place calls to mind. Not-this-word names it; execution true of line 49.

'round' is the next word on line 49 and is true there; the child answers with the wrong word of the phrase. Within-span-wrong-element names it. ('rather fat' is padding the execution does not claim from the text.)
Waving is no sense of 'made fast' and no lookalike word; not-this-word names it. Line 63 checked.
The rope is line 59, a true boat detail from an earlier part; the stem points to line 65. Wrong-scope names it. Execution true (unfastens, hauls, then steps in).

The animals talk throughout (rabbit line 22; Mole 57, 66-67; Rat 54, 64): the passage states the contrary of 'quiet, still and dull'. Contradicted-by-the-text names a lost claim, not a lost word. Execution lines checked.

The option is the GROUP sense of 'party' (people) at the wrong extent, not the social-gathering sense: nothing in 'Everybody who came to the assembly that night' is a celebration. The dominant-sense story is fitted to it, and the dominant-sense seat on this row is already the celebration option. The mistake is the scope of the group (all attendees vs the five at lines 21-22), which this entry does not name.

The first report (lines 17-18) is inside the window and true as a report; it answers 'what was reported' not 'who actually came in'. Within-span-wrong-element names it. It is earlier, not later, so chronology-collapse was misfiled.

en-technique-structure-effect-blind as written names one mistake: paraphrasing a SHORT SENTENCE where the answer is that its shortness makes the moment land. Three successive reports of a shrinking number are not sentence shape or length, and 'To make sure the reader counts the guests carefully' is not a paraphrase of content; it is an invented purpose aimed at the reader. The execution generalises the entry ('what their pattern does') beyond its description. If the entry is meant to cover sequence/pattern devices, its description must say so first.
'county' resembles 'countenance' in form; the meaning given belongs to that word. Form-lookalike names it.
'count' is taken out of 'countenance' and summed into a meaning. Built-from-parts names it.

Line 30 has the ladies declare him much handsomer than Mr Bingley: the passage states the contrary of the option. A reversed comparison is a contradicted claim, not an agent-patient swap. Execution true (manners at 31-33).
Lines 41-42 have him 'speaking occasionally to one of his own party': the passage states the contrary of 'said nothing to anybody'. Execution true.

A general dislike of proud people is a motive the passage never gives Mrs Bennet; lines 45-46 give her particular reason. Motive-invention names it; the passage does go as far as 'proudest' (42), so extreme-option-pull was misfiled.
She sits down at line 47 for want of gentlemen; Mr Darcy's remark is at lines 65-67 while she is already sitting. A later event given as the cause of an earlier one is exactly chronology-collapse.
Lines 48-49 give a conversation between Mr Darcy and Mr Bingley overheard because he stood near her; that states the contrary of speaking loudly to the whole room. Execution true.
'fast' is a different word at the start of 'fastidious'; the meaning given is that word's. Form-lookalike names it.
Rude is no sense of 'fastidious' and no lookalike's; not-this-word names it. 'coldly said' is line 66, checked.
Kind/easy-going is no sense of 'tolerable' and no lookalike's. Not-this-word names it.
'Putting up with things' is the meaning of TOLERANT, a different word of near form. Form-lookalike names it.
Lines 66-67 'not handsome enough to tempt me' state the contrary of 'very good-looking'. Contradicted-by-the-text names it.
Pride is Mr Darcy's (line 32 'discovered to be proud') moved onto Elizabeth, whom 'tolerable' describes. Attribute-transfer names it.
The praise of his looks belongs to the room (29 gentlemen, 30 ladies), moved onto Elizabeth, whom line 70 leaves 'with no very cordial feelings'. Attribute-transfer names it.

Minimal-pair-skim requires the differing detail to make the option wrong. It does not: the passage DOES show what the characters do and leaves the verdict to them (Bingley 'danced every dance' line 37, 'Such amiable qualities must speak for themselves' line 38-39; Darcy 'danced only once', walking about, lines 39-42; his remark at 65-69). 'We are shown what they do, but never told whether the writer approves' is true of the passage, so the execution's claim that the child has missed something is false of the row.
'A tool for seeing far away' is the meaning of telescope, a different word containing 'scope'. Nothing is summed from parts, so form-lookalike, not built-from-parts. Execution true of line 15.
'Painted so they could be seen' is no sense of 'substantial' and no lookalike's. Not-this-word names it; nothing is copied, so inference-literal-lookalike was misfiled.
The broken bridge is shouted by a different man at line 47, a true detail from another part; the stem names lines 10-11 and asks for no cause. Wrong-scope names it.
Line 10 'the river was rising fast' states the contrary of 'falling'. 'Rising' is a content word, not a relation word, so contradicted-by-the-text, not relation-word-flipped. Execution true.

Judgement call checked. 'bait' and 'wait' differ by one letter, and line 15 ('engaged him a long time') makes a long wait feel right; read as 'a good wait' the option follows. The meaning given is that of the lookalike word. Form-lookalike names it; the old plausible-not-stated did not (line 14 'good' rules it out, so it is not plausible).

Bait as a lure or enticement used to make someone do something is a genuine sense of the word, distinct from the fishing bait on the dominant-sense option; 'When we got to the town ... I had a good bait' (line 14) fixes feeding. Neighbouring-sense names it.
The broken bridge is line 47, another place and time; no cause is asked. Wrong-scope names it.
Line 29 'we can't drive over that tree' carries an explicit negative; the option states the affirmative. Negation-dropped names it exactly.
Leading the horse home on foot is sensible and nobody suggests it; lines 29-31 give the crossways plan and 'the horse is fresh'. Plausible-not-stated names it.

The execution says the passage denies the master the knowledge; at line 62 he HAS it ('if your Black Beauty had not been wiser than we were'). 'The master knew that Beauty was right to stop on the bridge' carries no time, so it is contradicted only on the bridge and true at the hall door, which the stem itself sends the child to. Contradicted-by-the-text holds under one reading only.

The execution says 'the passage never makes fear what stops him', but Beauty says 'I dare not go forward' and 'I dare not stir' (lines 36-38): not daring is fear. What the passage does not give is fear OF THE WATER; the execution's claim as written is false of the row.
Line 51 'the wind seemed to have lulled off' states the contrary of a worsening storm. Contradicted-by-the-text names it; no relation word is involved.
The writer's repeated wording is turned into a state in Beauty (tiredness); lines 51-52 describe the evening. The writer's choice read as the character's state is what the entry names.
Lines 55-58 and 62 credit the horse; 'badly trained' is the contrary claim. Contradicted-by-the-text names it.
Blame is a likely subject and lines 54-58 give none. Plausible-not-stated names it (no motive is involved).
The lull is line 51, a true detail before the talk at 53-58. Wrong-scope names it.
The limit Beauty gives is understanding (line 54 'I could not understand much'); fear as what stops him following speech is supplied. Plausible-not-stated names it.
Mixing is the commonest sense of 'stir' and 'I dare not stir' (line 37) fixes moving. Dominant-sense names it.
Making a sound is no sense of 'stir' and no lookalike's. Not-this-word names it.
A slow, careful piece of work is no sense of 'commotion' (near its reverse) and no lookalike's. Not-this-word names it; there is no relation word, so relation-word-flipped was misfiled.

Judgement call checked. 'motion' is plainly visible inside 'commotion' and 'com' reads as 'come'; summed, people coming and moving in at once. The parts are real and the sum is not the word, which is what built-from-parts names. Attribute-transfer was misfiled (nothing moves between holders).
Step-ladder and chair are called for at line 12, outside lines 8-9; no cause asked. Wrong-scope names it.
The measuring is line 38, a true detail from much later; it is stated, so plausible-not-stated was misfiled. Wrong-scope names it.
At line 13 the leg is Mr Goggles's; the option gives it to Pa. A detail moved to the wrong holder is attribute-transfer; nothing about doing/being done-to is reversed.
The crooked picture is line 58, from another part; no cause asked. Wrong-scope names it.
Lines 26-27 have the whole family standing round 'ready to help'; 'too busy to watch' is the contrary claim. Contradicted-by-the-text names it.

Judgement call checked. The question is about a SHAPE (counting a second, a third, a fourth, a fifth), and the answer is what that shape does (the crowd builds with every word). The option reads the content of the list (each helper has a job) as orderliness. That is 'reading content where the question asks about shape', the mechanism the entry names, with the entry's short-sentence case as its example. Contrast pp-07, where the key is about what the numbers mean, not their form.

The likelier pull is the ordinals themselves: 'a second, a third, a fourth, a fifth' read as steps in time, which lines 27-29 invite on their own. Nothing points to the child fetching half an hour (line 24) or midnight (line 58); the wrong-scope story is fitted to the option. The fault is reading the count as a sequence of stages, which is closer to the structure entry than to retrieval scope.
'as a rule' (a habit, a regular practice) is a genuine sense of 'rule'; line 38 'take the rule, and re-measure' fixes the measuring tool decisively. Neighbouring-sense names it.

The chair is line 42, outside lines 43-45; he slides from it on to the piano (44). Answering with the thing he was on rather than where he lands is a detail from outside the named lines. Wrong-scope names it.
The corns are line 61, at the end, his foot not his fall. Wrong-scope names it; no cause asked.
She never offers to do the job; it is a likely thing to say. Plausible-not-stated names it; nothing is reversed.
Having a man in is Uncle Podger's line at 62-63, said in scorn, moved onto Aunt Maria. Attribute-transfer names it; it is not a later cause.
Line 62 'evident pride' and 'some people would have had a man in to do a little thing like that' state the contrary of having learned the job was hard. Contradicted-by-the-text names it.

The option's feeling label is not what is wrong: 'He is pleased' is near-true of 'evident pride' (line 62). What is wrong is the OBJECT of the feeling, gladness at the family's help, which line 37 ('call us all fools') and line 52 ('you women, you make such a fuss') state the contrary of. Emotion-label-approximation does not name that; en-contradicted-by-the-text (as the reviewer note proposed) does.
The chlorine smell is line 5, the cupboard, not a sorting rule; the stem names lines 7-9. Wrong-scope names it; nothing is copied as a lookalike inference.
No feeling is evidenced in his flat, on-the-job replies (17, 21-22); annoyance is supplied, not approximated. Plausible-not-stated names it.
Friday is the collection day at line 8, carried in from lines 7-9 where the stem names 24-26. Wrong-scope names it; no second sorting is a later real event, so chronology-collapse was misfiled.
Lines 30-32 say he knew whose it was before he turned the collar out; the option states the contrary. Contradicted-by-the-text names it.
The Friday box is the jumper's destination (33) given to the paper. A detail moved between things is attribute-transfer; no cause or character is swapped.
Friday belongs to the charity collection (8-9) and is moved onto the annexe cupboard. Attribute-transfer names it.
Line 40 'You've missed a cupboard ... There's another one' states the contrary of 'already cleared'. Contradicted-by-the-text names it.
Whitby is line 19, Ilya's earlier talk; the stem names 40-41. Wrong-scope names it.

Judgement call checked. The option keeps the key's shape (nothing from inside Reuben, one other source) and changes the one detail to Ilya's talk; Ilya speaks of lockers (15), Whitby (19) and the annexe (40-41), never of Reuben, and 'only' drops Reuben's own actions. Minimal-pair-skim names it; nothing is a cause or agent swap.

The technique asked about is withheld interiority displaced into handled objects, a point-of-view choice, not sentence shape or length, which is what en-technique-structure-effect-blind names (its case is the short sentence landing suddenly). And the option is not a paraphrase of content: 'He describes only the old clothes, and so we get nothing else' is false of the passage, which also gives Ilya's talk, Miss Bhatt, the noticeboard (37-39) and the folded paper (35-36). The fault is a claim the text contradicts, or an overstatement ('only', 'nothing else'), not shape-blindness.

Passage stream-b-04 (row carries no passageRef). Lines 10-11 give the speed to Ilya while Reuben reads each collar, and line 14's 'anyway' makes the returns-box choice deliberate: the passage states the contrary of 'working faster ... made a mistake'. Contradicted-by-the-text names it; no relation word is flipped.

Passage stream-b-04. Miss Bhatt handles the jumper only at lines 43-49; the stem names lines 33-34. Wrong-scope names it; no cause is asked, so chronology-collapse was misfiled. (Line 48 'the way he had folded it' makes 'Folded it' true of Reuben; the option is wrong on 'gave it to Miss Bhatt', which the execution correctly locates.)

The tag is right (Roberta gives no view of the garden; a low opinion is supplied), but the execution puts 'not yet' in quotation marks as Roberta's words and they are not on the row: line 18 reads "We mustn't think of the garden yet". An execution's quoted words must be on the row; correct the quotation and re-propose.

Lines 3-5: the brooklet overflowed 'some days since' and is 'now congealed'. The option keeps the frozen brook and changes one detail, when it froze. Minimal-pair-skim names it; no real later event exists, so chronology-collapse was misfiled.
Lines 30-32 give the dog a purpose ('no other help at hand to summon'); fright is supplied. Plausible-not-stated names it; no evidenced feeling exists for fright to approximate.
Line 48 answers only with a charge 'like breakages'; worry is a kindly feeling supplied, with no evidenced feeling for it to approximate. Plausible-not-stated names it.

Line 55 has them say they are 'not afraid of ghosts'; the option changes that one detail to 'no ghost'. Minimal-pair-skim names it; nothing is copied as an inference lookalike. ('That is all nonsense', line 34, is said once by Washington about the stain; it does not make 'keep saying, over and over' true.)
Lines 14-15 give Tom's own reason (she can't play bandy); jealousy is supplied with no evidenced feeling. Plausible-not-stated names it.
The stem asks why; lines 48-49 give his reason (fairness owed back), and jealousy of her pleasure is an invented motive. Motive-invention names it.
Line 49 'He would have refused a bit of hers beforehand' states the contrary; 'refused' is a content word, not a relation word. Contradicted-by-the-text names it.
Lines 20-22: 'the most goes for rum' is other men; 'I puts it all away' is Silver. The option gives Silver the spending the speech denies. Contradicted-by-the-text names it.

Lines 11-12 'I would not have shown myself for all the world, but lay there' and 52-53 (no strength to leap out) state the contrary of going to warn anyone. Contradicted-by-the-text names it; no motive is the fault.
'Careful' is the meaning of CAUTIOUS, a different word of near form; nothing is summed from parts. Form-lookalike names it.

Passage stream-a-08-christmas-carol (row carries no passageRef). Scrooge is alone throughout and searches the rooms himself (32-37); sending for someone is a likely course the passage never states. Plausible-not-stated names it; no motive is the fault.
Line 49 'I prefer Dr Johnson to Mr Boz' and line 41 (the Captain defending Boz's style) state the contrary of both halves. Contradicted-by-the-text names it; no relation word.
Line 18 ('It is quite a different sort of thing') is inside the window and is what he SAYS; line 20 is what he ASKS. Within-span-wrong-element names it; no cause is asked.

Lines 36-37 'in a low voice, which I think Miss Jenkyns could not have heard' state the contrary of wanting the whole company to hear. Contradicted-by-the-text names it; there is no negative word to drop, so negation-dropped would not fit either.
'Not able to be excused' is the meaning of INEXCUSABLE, a different word of near form. Form-lookalike names it.
Line 24 has her staying in the house; nowhere does she say she wrote anything. Plausible-not-stated names it; an invented action, not a motive.
Lines 22-23 are inside the window and are what she is TOLD to do; lines 21-22 are what the mother EXPECTS. Within-span-wrong-element names it; no relation word is flipped.

The option's content is ON the line: line 34 gives 'the contemplation of errands to be done in the great metropolis of Milltown' as one of the things that lulled him, so thinking about the errands is true inside the window and is the cause of the state rather than the state. That is the same within-span-wrong-element shape as the sibling option 'Being lulled by the heat and dust'. Not-this-word treats the option as a meaning plucked from nowhere, and the execution's 'takes the errands as what fills Mr Cobb's mind' implies a falsehood the line does not support.
Line 39 is inside the window and is what he saw after turning; line 37 is what he first took the voice for. Within-span-wrong-element names it; no cause is asked.

Passage stream-a-21-rebecca-sunnybrook (row carries no passageRef). Paying is not a sense of 'passenger' (a traveller in a vehicle who is not its driver or crew); it is an association, so the execution's 'the everyday sense of passenger, someone who has paid to travel' asserts a sense the word does not have, and dominant-sense requires 'a real sense of the same word'. The likelier pull is on the row itself: the mother 'paid the fare' (16), Rebecca asks 'Does it cost any more?' (45), 'no extry charge' (50).

Passage stream-a-20-bevis (row carries no passageRef). Lines 3 and 5 'No, you go' / 'I shan't' and line 6 (the tench fades away) state the contrary of Mark running for the rod while the fish waited. Contradicted-by-the-text names it; nobody runs, so chronology-collapse was misfiled.

'Inclined' as bent or leaning is a genuine sense; line 45 'almost felt inclined to leave it and run round' fixes wanting decisively. Neighbouring-sense names it; the word does not contain 'lean', so built-from-parts was misfiled.
The ledge is found at lines 57-58, outside 49-54; Pan comes back of his own accord (50-51). Wrong-scope names the ledge; no cause is asked.

Line 29 'yours would have been hard and stale by then'; the option keeps the staleness and changes one detail, would-have to had-already. Minimal-pair-skim names it; the staling never happens, so chronology-collapse was misfiled.
'press' is visible inside 'suppress' and summed into pressing down; the part is real and the sum is not the word's meaning at line 38. Built-from-parts names it; nothing figurative is read literally.

Line 46 risks the twenty thousand at Baring's and line 74 calls it 'half of his fortune'; 'everything ... down to the last penny' is the all-or-nothing overreach. Extreme-option-pull names it; it is stated and overstated, not unstated.
'scrape' is a different word 'scruples' resembles in form; the meaning given is that word's. Form-lookalike names it; nothing figurative is read literally.

Contradicted-by-the-text needs the passage to deny the option. The only denial is the speaker's own 'Nobody put me there' (line 7), and this item's whole reading, by its own techniqueKey 'a-choice-insisted-on-against-the-picking-that-produced-it', is that the speaker's claim is undercut by the picking (line 38). An option that says he was effectively picked for goal is close to that subtext, not contradicted by it; the execution treats an unreliable speaker's claim as the text's fact.

Line 69 'Rikki-tikki had never met a live cobra before' states the contrary of Nag fearing him on the day of the flood (lines 8-12). Contradicted-by-the-text names it; no real later event is involved.

Passage stream-a-15-jungle-book (row carries no passageRef). Lines 15-16 wrap Rikki-tikki in cotton wool and warm him over a little fire; the option carries that care across to the nest, helped by the cotton at line 49. Attribute-transfer names the moved detail; it is a splice of two holders, not a single detail from the wrong part.
Lines 66-67 (she 'had cherished her anger till it grew strong') and 73 ('let her take care of herself') state the contrary of having forgotten. Contradicted-by-the-text names it.
Lines 53-55 give Meg's condition (Jo good-natured with Laurie, then a quiet minute); Laurie going home is a likely condition she never gives. Plausible-not-stated names it; no motive is involved.

Music swelling (growing louder) is a genuine sense but not the commonest; the key's 'gets bigger' is. Lines 3-4 (wood swells, doors stop shutting) fix size decisively. Neighbouring-sense names it; dominant-sense was misfiled.
breeze -> gale goes up in strength; shower -> drizzle goes down. The relation applied backwards is exactly vr03-reversed-relation.
'swift' covers promptness (a swift reply); 'early' tilts that area to before-time rather than speed. Wrong-shade names it; it is a meaning neighbour, not mere co-occurrence.
Heaviness is a property huge things often have, not a tilt of 'huge'. One-feature-only names it (the entry's own example shape).
Thinness is one property that can go with letting light through, not what 'transparent' means. One-feature-only names it.
Shiny co-occurs with transparent in talk of glass and plastic without sharing its meaning. Keeps-the-same-company names it.
'gentle' turns up beside 'melancholy' in talk of soft music and does not mean sad. Keeps-the-same-company names it.

rows.reason: Retag attested, but the row fails the child-facing gate on a PRE-EXISTING fault the retag did not touch: "arms" (option 'Resting his aching back and weary arms.') is routed HOLD AND ROUTE by the subject-matter rule. Content otherwise stands: key is the only answer to lines 1 to 4.

Checked lines 14-15: key is the only place stated; bank (36), gap (22), boat (60), carriage-drive (10, a comparison) all wrong. Pre-existing en-evidence-vividness-bias on the boat option is a library-attestation gate, not a content fault.
Lines 22-23: key (sixpence for the private road) is the only answer; spring-cleaning, boat ride (63), being let past, onion-sauce (25, a jeer) all wrong.

Seat refused: the option 'An argument between two of the rabbits.' would carry no correctly filed tag. The key stands (noise and fuss the Mole made) and the option is wrong on its parties, but the row cannot be signed with a misfiled seat. LIVE.
Line 29 makes 'A river' the only answer; meadow, the river-as-animal (line 30 is the river), face with whiskers (48) and sunshine are wrong.
Key (river seems alive, playful, always moving) is the only purpose answer; literal animal, threat (line 30 'with a gurgle ... with a laugh'), Rat's hole (39) and the Mole's belief all wrong.

Key matches lines 34-36 (spell-bound, follows the river). Two options now under en-comparison-vehicle-misread (age, keeping pace) are distinct aspects of the same vehicle; no giveaway pattern. Other distractors wrong.
Line 43 'something bright and small seemed to twinkle' makes the key the only answer; star (44, a comparison), glow-worm (45, ruled out), ears and hair (51) wrong.

Key (reader sees the face appear bit by bit as the Mole does) is the only answer to the short-paragraph question; creeping closer, fear, meadow jumps (19), grandeur all wrong. Other options' library-attestation gates are not content faults.
Line 49 'A grave round face': key (serious and calm) is the only fitting sense; burial place, earth, sadness, roundness all wrong.
Line 63 'made fast': key (tied the boat up firmly) is the only answer; quickly, fasting, hurrying the Mole (64), waving all wrong.
Line 65 'stern': key (back part of the boat) is the only answer. Note: rope and oars now both carry en-wrong-scope-retrieval; distinct details, no giveaway.
Key checked: sixpence (22), house (1), boat (60); fur (4), paws (13), whiskers (48). Distractors all false of the text. Other option's library-attestation gate is not a content fault.
Seat refused: 'Everybody who came to the assembly that night.' would keep a misfiled tag. Key and distractors otherwise stand (lines 21-22 count the party as five). LIVE.
Lines 21-22 give the five; key is the only match. Two options (first and second reports) now share within-span-wrong-element: both are superseded reports; no answer-revealing pattern.
Seat refused: the option would keep a misfiled tag (en-repetition-purpose, no repetition here). Key and distractors otherwise stand. LIVE.
Lines 24 and 34 ('pleasant countenance', 'forbidding, disagreeable countenance') fix the face sense; key is the only answer. Neighbouring verb sense, manners (24-25), county and count all wrong.
Lines 30-35: key (behaved as if above everyone, lines 32-33) is the only cause; money (33 'large estate'), looks (30), ball closing early (Bingley, 37), disliked from the start (30) all wrong.

Key (room's quick opinion sounds settled) is the only answer about what the short, sure sentences do; the other options are a literal verdict, an invented writer motive, the decide-a-decision sense, and a contradicted claim.
Lines 44-46: key matches 'slighted one of her daughters'; introduction (40, other ladies), remark to Mr Bennet (absent), Bingley's dancing, and invented motive all wrong.
Line 47 'obliged, by the scarcity of gentlemen' makes the key the only answer; not wanting to dance, Darcy's refusal (later), wanting to listen (48 is chance), sister dancing (60) all wrong.
Key (reader hears the words when Elizabeth does) is the only answer to why she hears them first-hand; listening-in taste, emptied room (49 dance in progress), Bingley's plan, loud speech all wrong.
Lines 57-59 (choosy about partners, contrasted with 'so many pleasant girls') fix 'hard to please'; speed, shyness, tidiness (ruled out by context), rudeness all wrong.
Line 66 'tolerable: but not handsome enough' makes 'only just good enough to look at' the only answer; all four distractors wrong for distinct reasons, no shared tag, no pattern.
Lines 70-73 ('told the story ... with great spirit', 'delighted in anything ridiculous') make the key the only answer; forgiveness, sympathy, not bothered at all, admiration all wrong.

Two defensible answers: 'We are shown what they do, but never told whether the writer approves.' is as true of the passage as the key (lines 37-42 and 65-70 show conduct and the narrator gives no verdict of her own). A 9-11-year-old reading carefully can choose it on evidence. The option needs redrafting (Cowork) before the row can sign.
Lines 15-16 'more scope for imagination' make 'room for the mind to work' the only answer; cooler spot, quiet spot, telescope all wrong.
Line 8 'good substantial rails' fixes 'strong and solidly built'; large amount, new, painted all wrong.
Line 10 makes the key the only answer; broken bridge (47, another man), falling (contradicted), road shut (12 they drive through) all wrong.
Line 14 fixes 'a feed and a rest'; fishing bait (dominant), wait (lookalike), lure (neighbouring) all wrong, each under its own entry.
Lines 22-24 make the key the only answer; branch (20, John's worry), bridge (47), leaves (4) all wrong.
Lines 29-31 make the key the only answer ('go back to the four crossways ... a good six miles'); drive over, wait, lead home all wrong.
